title: Infection, demyelination, toxic and metabolic disease

steps.tx: A pyogenic **brain abscess** exhibits central **restricted diffusion** on diffusion-weighted imaging with marked hypointensity on apparent diffusion coefficient maps, reflecting high-viscosity cellular pus, debris, and inflammatory myeloperoxidase activity. The surrounding capsule demonstrates thin, smooth, T2 hypointense margins with ring enhancement on contrast T1 imaging, surrounded by vasogenic oedema.
steps.say: A pyogenic brain abscess exhibits central restricted diffusion on diffusion weighted imaging with marked hypointensity on apparent diffusion coefficient maps. High viscosity cellular pus, debris, and inflammatory myeloperoxidase activity cause this profound diffusion restriction. The surrounding collagenous capsule demonstrates thin, smooth, T2 hypointense margins with intense ring enhancement on contrast T1 weighted images, surrounded by prominent vasogenic oedema.

vis.caption: Brain abscess pathology and imaging features on MRI

steps.tx: **Herpes simplex virus** type 1 encephalitis classically produces asymmetric, fulminant swelling with FLAIR hyperintensity and diffusion restriction involving the **medial temporal** lobes, insular cortex, and inferior frontal gyri. Sparing of the lentiform nucleus and basal ganglia is a critical diagnostic landmark differentiating necrotizing viral encephalitis from middle cerebral artery infarction.

rows: Cortical swelling and gyral diffusion restriction
Preserved architecture rules out MCA ischemia

steps.tx: In **Multiple sclerosis**, demyelinating perivenular white matter lesions typically manifest as **Dawson fingers**, which extend perpendicularly from the callososeptal interface along deep medullary callososeptal venules. Sagittal FLAIR MRI provides optimal sensitivity for detecting these periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial demyelinating plaques satisfying McDonald criteria for spatial dissemination.

rows: Centrifugal spread into callososeptal white matter
Flame-shaped demyelinating plaque on sagittal FLAIR
Permanent callosal volume loss and T1 black holes

steps.tx: **Neuromyelitis optica** spectrum disorder presents with **longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis** characterized by contiguous T2 intramedullary hyperintensity extending across 3 or more vertebral segments. Central cord predominance, extensive cord swelling, and serum **aquaporin-4** IgG autoantibodies establish the diagnosis, contrasting with the short-segment, peripheral, dorsal cord lesions typical of multiple sclerosis.

right.title: Multiple Sclerosis

steps.tx: **Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome** manifests as bilateral, symmetrical **vasogenic** subcortical white matter oedema predominantly distributed across the parieto-occipital regions. Triggered by acute hypertension, pre-eclampsia, or calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, autoregulatory breakthrough preferentially affects posterior vascular territories while sparing the calcarine and paramedian occipital cortex.

steps.tx: **Osmotic demyelination syndrome** occurs following rapid correction of profound chronic hyponatraemia, precipitating oligodendrocyte swelling and symmetrical intramyelinic oedema within the **central pons**. MRI demonstrates classic trident-shaped or bat-wing T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity with restricted diffusion in the pontine base, strictly sparing the peripheral tegmentum and ventrolateral corticospinal tracts.

left.title: Central Pontine Myelinolysis
points: High T2 and restricted diffusion on ADC

steps.tx: **Wernicke encephalopathy** develops secondary to severe **thiamine** deficiency, impairing cerebral glucose utilization and pyruvate dehydrogenase decarboxylation. Symmetrical T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity selectively involves the **mammillary bodies**, medial dorsomedial thalamic nuclei, periaqueductal grey matter, and tectal plate, frequently accompanied by contrast enhancement of the mammillary bodies.

steps.tx: In prion diseases, sporadic **Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease** exhibits pathognomonic **cortical ribboning** on diffusion-weighted imaging and FLAIR alongside restricted diffusion in the caudate heads and putamen. In contrast, variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease classically displays bilateral thalamic hyperintensity producing the pulvinar and hockey-stick signs where pulvinar signal intensity exceeds that of the anterior striatum.

steps.tx: Acute **Wernicke encephalopathy** is an underdiagnosed clinical emergency requiring immediate high-dose parenteral **thiamine** supplementation prior to administering intravenous glucose infusions. Characteristic cranial MRI features demonstrate symmetric hyperintensity on T2-weighted and FLAIR sequences with swelling of the **mammillary bodies**, medial thalamic nuclei, and periaqueductal gray matter alongside prominent contrast enhancement.
